See also: ídolo

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Derived from Old French idole, from Latin īdōlum (“image, form”), from Ancient Greek εἴδωλον (eídōlon), from εἶδος (eîdos, “form, shape”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /iˈdolo/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -olo
  • Syllabification: i‧do‧lo

Noun

[edit]

idolo (accusative singular idolon, plural idoloj, accusative plural idolojn)

  1. idol (false god)
  2. idol (venerated object or person)

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Esperanto idolo, English idol, French idole, German Idol, Italian idolo, Russian и́дол (ídol), Spanish ídolo, most from Latin īdōlum (except Russian), all from Ancient Greek εἴδωλον (eídōlon).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /iˈdo.lo/

Noun

[edit]

idolo (plural idoli)

  1. (also figurative) idol (venerated object, person or idea)

idolo m (plural idoli)

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish ídolo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ˈʔidolo/ [ˌʔiː.d̪oˈlo]
  • Rhymes: -idolo
  • Syllabification: i‧do‧lo

Noun

[edit]

ídoló (Baybayin spelling ᜁᜇᜓᜎᜓ)

  1. idol (graven image of anything worshipped)
  2. idol (person that one looks up to)
    Synonym: (slang) lodi

Derived terms

[edit]
  • idolohin

Related terms

[edit]
  • idolatra
  • idolatrahin
  • idolatriya
